strengths: Addresses a well-documented and frustrating practical problem (BF16+FA failure) that has remained unsolved for years in the community
Provides detailed mechanistic analysis through systematic ablations, effectively isolating the specific components responsible for failure
Clear decomposition of root causes into two related phenomena: low-rank representation similarity and biased BF16 rounding, with supporting visualizations
Rigorous mathematical treatment of BF16 arithmetic and rounding error accumulation, including concrete numerical examples
Proposes a minimal, mathematically-motivated, and practical fix that successfully stabilizes training in the demonstrated case
Well-structured presentation that traces failure causality through a clear chain of reasoning (Figure 1)
weaknesses: Extremely limited scope: analysis restricted to single model (GPT-2 12L), single architecture, single dataset, single hyperparameter configuration; generalization is completely unaddressed
Proposed fix is narrowly tailored to this specific failure mode; unclear if it addresses other FA instabilities or whether it benefits practitioners already using standard stabilization techniques

Insufficient experimental validation of the solution: only loss curves shown, no downstream metrics, no computational cost analysis, no comparison with existing stabilization methods, single run with no confidence intervals
Causal mechanism between the two root causes is underspecified: why similar low-rank representations emerge mechanistically is unexplained, and the dependency between causes is not formalized
Limited novelty: mechanistic analysis is primarily empirical forensics on one failure case; the fix is a straightforward practical patch rather than a fundamental insight into low-precision training
Critical question unanswered: why Flash Attention specifically is vulnerable compared to standard attention remains unclear, limiting understanding of which settings are truly affected
Incomplete related work engagement: many existing stabilization techniques could address this, but systematic comparison and explanation of why this case requires a new solution is missing
Unclear practical significance: limited evidence that BF16+FA is a common combination practitioners encounter, or that this failure mode is frequent relative to alternatives already in use

strengths: Addresses a real, well-documented failure case affecting practitioners (nanoGPT issues), providing the first mechanistic explanation for catastrophic loss explosions in BF16 training with flash attention
Systematic and thorough root cause analysis with methodical ablations that isolate the failure to flash attention layer 2, specific attention heads, and the δ computation in the P·V product
Clear mathematical exposition showing how biased rounding errors in BF16 arithmetic and similar low-rank representations interact to create error accumulation cycles that corrupt training dynamics

Elegant and minimal solution that leverages the shift-invariance property of softmax to ensure P elements remain less than 1, preventing negative values and overflow—mathematically principled and practical
Strong empirical validation across multiple hardware platforms (NVIDIA A100, RTX 4090, Huawei Ascend) with effective visualizations that make complex analysis accessible (Figures 1, 3-6)
Well-structured presentation with clear analytical flow and comprehensive related work positioning the contribution appropriately in the low-precision training literature
weaknesses: Limited scope: analysis is specific to GPT-2 + Flash Attention + BF16; generalization to larger models, other architectures (ViT, BERT), and other low-precision formats (FP8, INT8) remains unexplored and unclear
Uses mixed-precision training (BF16 forward, FP32 backward) rather than pure low-precision training; applicability to pure BF16 or other emerging formats not established

Analysis is primarily post-hoc explanation rather than predictive theory; the causal link between spectral norm growth and training failure is correlational, and the theory cannot predict when/where similar failures will occur

Lacks comparative evaluation: no experiments comparing the proposed fix to existing stabilization techniques (loss scaling, gradient clipping, careful initialization), limiting evidence of relative merit
Hyperparameter selection for β lacks principled guidance (used β ∈ [2,8] without ablation or sensitivity analysis); no clear guidance for practitioners on setting β for different configurations
Limited experimental scope: only evaluates loss curves on a single dataset (OpenWebText) without downstream task validation or analysis of potential side effects from the modification
Numerical examples in Section 3.3.2 appear cherry-picked to illustrate the problem; unclear how representative they are of typical failure scenarios and whether conclusions generalize broadly
Code availability mentioned but link appears missing from submitted paper, limiting reproducibility; some hyperparameter details also incomplete
Paper reads more as 'bug analysis with fix' than methodological contribution; the modification is a targeted workaround rather than a general principle for designing low-precision training systems

strengths: Addresses a real, well-documented practical problem (flash attention + BF16 instability) that remained unresolved for two years, providing the first mechanistic explanation
Thorough and systematic investigation with carefully designed experiments to isolate failure sources (disabling tiling, replacing components, swapping precision levels)
Clear mathematical exposition with detailed derivations showing how errors propagate through attention computation and accumulate in specific patterns
Provides reproducible methodology for diagnosing similar numerical failures and validates findings across multiple hardware platforms
Offers a simple, mathematically justified solution to the softmax computation that stabilizes training across different optimizer configurations
Effective visualizations (spectral norms, error accumulation patterns, token differences) that clearly illustrate the structural mechanisms of failure
weaknesses: Limited novelty: This is fundamentally a post-hoc debugging analysis and bug fix rather than a novel algorithmic or methodological contribution suitable for a top-tier venue

Extremely narrow scope: Analysis is highly specific to GPT-2 (tiny 12-layer model) with BF16 and flash attention; unclear how it generalizes to other architectures, model scales, or precision formats (FP8, INT8)

Insufficient experimental validation: Main experiments use toy models with very short training runs (100-6000 steps); no validation on realistic scales or on the original failure case (nanoGPT large-scale training)

Incomplete root cause analysis: Two causes identified but their relative importance is not quantified; unclear how similar low-rank matrices and rounding bias interact; why QK-clipping and other techniques fail here is unexplained

Limited practical impact: The fix is a narrow patch for one specific failure mode; practitioners have simpler workarounds (use FP32 or standard attention); unclear if this would be adopted in practice

Sparse validation of the proposed solution: The fix is only tested on GPT-2S for very short runs (100 steps in Fig. 7); no demonstration that it prevents the actual loss explosion at scale on the original failure case

Presentation issues: Paper is dense with heavy notation that obscures insights; the main contribution (softmax modification) is buried in technical details; weak motivation for why this specific failure deserves detailed study

Generalizability concerns: Appendix D shows similar patterns in Llama-3.1-8B but the proposed fix is not validated there; no exploration of applicability to other low-precision formats or architectural variations
Reproducibility ambiguities: Unclear whether the failure is deterministic or probabilistic; the specific conditions triggering failure vs. stability are not fully characterized

strengths: Addresses a real, well-documented failure case that has plagued practitioners for over two years with a rigorous root cause analysis
Provides novel mechanistic insights: the interplay between low-rank representation emergence and BF16 rounding bias is well-explained with concrete mathematical derivations and binary representations
Systematic and methodical diagnosis approach: clearly isolates failure to a specific layer and operation through targeted experiments
Practical solution that works: proposed modification is simple, mathematically justified, and demonstrated to stabilize training on both GPT-2 and Llama models
Excellent presentation with clear figures (especially Figures 1, 5, 6) that effectively communicate complex failure mechanisms
Provides a diagnostic framework that could be applied to detect similar numerical instabilities in other low-precision settings
Good reproducibility: clear experimental setup, hyperparameter details, and promise of code release
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: only demonstrates fix on 2B and 6.3B parameter models; behavior on much larger models unclear, and no computational overhead analysis provided

Missing comparative evaluation: no direct experimental comparison with alternative stabilization approaches (gradient scaling, loss scaling, higher precision operations) that might also address this problem
Insufficient ablation studies: does not justify specific threshold choices (e.g., why [2,8]?) or explore sensitivity to these parameters
Limited algorithmic novelty: the core contribution is a targeted normalization adjustment rather than a fundamental algorithmic innovation; primarily an engineering fix rather than a novel method

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: while low-rank emergence is documented empirically, the paper lacks deep explanation for why flash attention specifically triggers this phenomenon or whether it could occur in other contexts
Narrow validation scope: evaluation focuses on the specific failure case; unclear if fix works for other problematic configurations or under varying hyperparameter regimes

Scope limitations acknowledged but not fully addressed: solution is specific to softmax in flash attention; generalization to other low-precision formats (FP8, INT8) or other architectures remains unclear
Implementation details missing: practitioners would benefit from clearer guidance on threshold selection and conditions for triggering the fix in diverse settings
